The Game of Life

AlgorithmsCountingLogic
Game: Cells live, die and are born by three simple rules. There is no winning — just patterns.
How to play: Click cells to draw, choose a pattern or randomize, then run or step through generations.

Look for the math

Conway's Life is not a game to win — it is a cellular automaton whose simple rules create astonishing behaviour.

Three rules

A live cell with two or three live neighbours survives; otherwise it dies. An empty cell with exactly three live neighbours comes alive. Everything happens simultaneously from one generation to the next.

Patterns

A block never changes; a blinker, toad and beacon flip between two states; a glider travels one cell diagonally every four generations. Such patterns can be combined to build logic gates, so Life is capable of universal computation. The logic test checks these patterns, the birth and survival rules, and that a reverse step restores the previous generation.

Place two gliders so they collide. What survives the crash?
